newsitem.title: MONACO: Monaco's low-key birthday prompts big global yawn.
newsitem.headline: Monaco's low-key birthday prompts big global yawn.

text.p: The imminent launch of a 10-month party marking the 700th birthday of the tiny principality of Monaco is generating a big global yawn.

Apart from Monaco's royal family, which claims to be the longest-reigning European dynasty, the highest-ranking celebrity expected to attend Wednesday's opening ceremonies is the Vatican spokesman, festival organisers said.
A day before the launch, the streets were virtually deserted, hotels had plenty of vacancies and festival decorations consisted largely of recycled Christmas lighting.
The principality's top-ranked restaurant, the ultra-costly Louis XV, was curiously closed down on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"They'll be celebrating the birthday on Thursday," offered the doorman at the luxury Hotel de Paris, where the Louis XV is located.

"This is not a festival but a commemoration," said Isabelle Peters, spokeswoman for the event. "The Prince (Rainier III) wanted the celebration to be between the princely family and the people of Monaco."

The little country, on the Mediterranean coast and surrounded by France, can be walked from end-to-end in half an hour. Even so, Peters said, many of its 30,000 people are likely to stay at home on Wednesday, watching the party live on cable television.

The celebration starts on Wednesday morning with a mass, followed by the dedication of a statue by Kees Verkade, a waterfront re-enactment of the principality's past glories and a concert by the Monte Carlo ballet and opera companies.
All of the events are to take place, as the organisers put it, "in the presence of the princely family".
The family has been in the public eye more or less constantly since Rainier married the American movie star Grace Kelly in 1956.
In addition to white-haired Rainier, 73, who has reigned since May 1949, there are his son Prince Albert, slightly balding at 38, and the striking Princesses Caroline, 39, and Stephanie, 31.
Monaco is probably best known around the world from the succession of glossy cover pictures of the photogenic family.
But it has had a bad run of luck since Grace's death in a 1982 car crash, all of it amply documented by Monaco's paparazzi.

Stephanie's most recent cover appearances followed the publication in Italy of photographs of her now ex-husband Daniel Ducruet cavorting with "Miss Topless Belgium", Fily Houteman, at a Riviera poolside.
The couple, who have two children, were divorced in October, a few weeks after the pictures appeared.

Caroline, believed to be the first princess ever photographed topless, appeared completely bald in her latest cover shots. She has not publicly explained the phenomenon though she has willingly posed for pictures.
Albert, typically photographed with the likes of Claudia Schiffer, Brooke Shields and Lisa-Marie Presley, is coordinating Monaco's birthday party at his father's request.
Rainier is grooming him to take over the tiny state but seems in no hurry to step down despite major heart surgery two years ago.
"I'm waiting for my son to feel ready to take over," Rainier said in a recent interview. "I don't want a brutal abdication. It must be done smoothly".
